blocks.x: Dior Sauvage is one of the most popular colognes of all time. You know it, you've smelled it, and there's a strong chance someone in your life is wearing it as we speak. But sometimes, its fame can distract from the rest of Dior’s fragrance offering. And that’s a shame, especially when there’s a lesser-known Dior fragrance line with better ingredients, more elegant formulations, and—for those, like me, who care—much more beautiful bottle designs.

La Collection Privée (literally, "private collection") is essentially Dior's olfactory couture line. It’s an idea that goes right back to Christian Dior himself, who saw himself as much a perfumer as a couturier. The initial LCP collection took shape in 2004, and its tie to perfumery royalty Francis Kurkdjian, now Dior's Perfume Creation Director, goes all the way back to that year: He created two of its three founding fragrances, Eau Noire and Cologne Blanche. Today, Kurkdjian approaches each new Privée like a couturier approaches a garment, creating what Dior calls an "olfactory silhouette," drawing on flowers (and even fabrics) from the house’s history.

That all sounds lofty, I know. But smell any Privée fragrance, and I feel you’ll quickly forgive me. Whether it's an OG like the woody, ambery, intoxicating Bois d'Argent, or a newer Kurkdjian creation like the gorgeous floral-leather Cuir Saddle, nothing in the line feels cluttered or busy, yet nothing feels too simple either. The richer scents have depth without being stifling, while the fresher ones are crisp without feeling thin. Together, the entire line has a cool, almost stark refinement.

The bottles match the mood: minimalist cylinders of crystal-clear glass, with clean lines and sleek black lacquer caps, a design that also dates back to 2004. Yes, you'll pay for the privilege of rocking a Privée, but damn if they don't smell and look the part.

So, which to choose? The collection runs all the way through from bright citrus to florals to green scents, but with cooler weather here, I lean towards the LCP scents that come alive when the temperature drops. The five below are scents for making a sophisticated impression wherever you are, and they make a heck of a holiday gift, too. Oh, and in my experience, they’re also serious compliment magnets.

blocks.x: Whenever I mention La Collection Privée to fellow fragrance nerds, someone inevitably says, “I love Gris Dior.” It’s a signature of the line, and a modern classic unto itself. The fragrance is a chypre—an industry term for a combination of light citrus on a more floral, woodsy foundation—and takes you on a beautiful, strange journey. Vetiver and labdanum give the rose woody depth, while the citrus opening adds brightness before everything settles into something mossy and almost damp with earth.

And yet, for all that richness, Gris Dior still wears pretty sheer and abstract. This is a fantastic first foray into Dior’s private line, refined enough for the workplace but intriguing enough for nighttime, too. Don’t be surprised if it becomes a signature in your rotation.

blocks.x: Oud can be a lot. Loud, sometimes downright funky, not to mention its distinctly potent scent-cloud aura. Thankfully, Dior’s all have something in common: they’re incredibly elegant, polished takes on a note that isn’t always either. With Oud Ispahan, rather than taming the eccentric qualities Oud admirers prize, Dior pairs them with velvety Damascus rose, creating a gorgeous push-pull between smoky and airy. It’s still unmistakably Oud, just wearing a Super 180s wool suit.

Underneath that rose-and-oud pairing, patchouli, sandalwood, and saffron add warmth, earthiness, and spice. It’s rich and woody, but there’s an almost sheer floral quality to it, an oud dressed for a black-tie soirée. There’s plenty of depth, but also this beautiful lift that keeps Oud Ispahan from ever feeling overwhelming. And while it may be refined, don’t think it’s shy. This is dinner, date night, and break-out-the-finest-coat territory, with the kind of staying power that means you’ll probably still catch a whiff on your cashmere sweater the next morning.

blocks.x: The leather fragrance family has a lot of range. You have your rustic, straight-off-the-ranch variety, your smoky, dimly-lit lounge variety, and plenty in between. Cuir Saddle is its own thing and, bar none, it’s one of the most elegant, addictive takes on the genre I’ve ever smelled. Inspired by Dior’s iconic Saddle Bag, with its asymmetrical, saddle-shaped design, the fragrance translates leather into something equally singular. This is skin-scent leather, almost suede-like in its smoothness, married with white florals that bring an airy freshness to the composition.

And despite all that refinement, Cuir Saddle is versatile. You could rock this on a crisp spring day or a winter night. There’s a noir quality to it I personally love, like something you’d wear walking through NYC on a mysterious rainy evening, yet it begs to be worn with tailoring for an event on a sunny day, too. The drydown is also a bit of a chameleon, with almost ambery undertones emerging to give all that softness some gravitas.

blocks.x: So here’s something cool that unites both Christian Dior and Francis Kurkdjian—both are associated with always having a lucky charm on their person. Dior famously carried a small piece of wood for good luck, while Kurkdjian keeps a sugar cube close at hand. Fittingly, those two talismans come together here as sensual woods and opulent vanilla, with an almost boozy warmth running through it all. The vanilla is very prominent, but decidedly grown-up: nothing remotely resembling baked goods, but rather rich and intoxicating.

Sultry, sophisticated, and belly-warming, this calls for plush textures, a shawl-collar cardigan, and wool flannel trousers as you relax at the end of a long working day. It’s a gentleman’s scent with the confidence to match and, in my opinion, Dior’s finest gourmand.

blocks.x: The Esprits de Parfum are essentially La Collection Privée’s push into even richer, more concentrated territory. And while the classic Bois d’Argent EDP strikes a near-perfect balance of powdery iris, woods, and smoky frankincense, the Esprit takes that DNA and makes it even moodier. A particularly rich Tuscan Iris brings powdery, old-school elegance; the frankincense takes on an almost honeyed warmth; and musk gives it warm-skin sensuality. That interplay of ambery warmth and powdery florals is what Kurkdjian uses to play up the Esprit’s skin-to-skin quality.

Saving the best until last, it may be my favorite fragrance in the entire Privée collection. The Esprit does, however, carry a heftier price tag, but it’s concentrated: a spray or two leaves a gorgeous wafting trail behind you.
